bartaWaterfalls.name: Barta Waterfalls
bartaWaterfalls.about:
Barta Waterfall is a hidden natural gem in Jordan, set within a rugged landscape of rocky cliffs and flowing water near Wadi Hidan. Its dramatic waterfall and scenic surroundings make it an exciting destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

Whether you're exploring the canyon, hiking along the trail, or capturing the beauty of the falls, Barta offers a chance to experience a wilder side of Jordan.

highlights.title: Explore the Canyon
highlights.description: Walk through the natural landscape and discover the water-carved rock formations along the route

highlights.title: Upper Waterfall Abseiling
highlights.description: Descend rocky cliffs and waterfalls using ropes and professional safety equipment, for an unforgettable canyon adventure.

highlights.title: Capture the Wild Beauty
highlights.description: Photograph the waterfall, rocky textures, and beautiful contrasts between water and stone.

packing: Bring a fully charged phone and power bank.
Bring a change of clothes if water crossings are expected.
bartaWaterfalls.safetyTip: Visit with an experienced local guide, check the weather and water levels, and avoid the canyon during rain or flash-flood warnings.

deadsea.name: Dead Sea
deadsea.about: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on Earth. Known for its high salt content, therapeutic mud and stunning views, it’s a perfect place to relax, float and enjoy the natural beauty.

petra.name: Petra
petra.about: Discover Petra, Jordan’s legendary Rose City, where ancient Nabataean architecture meets breathtaking natural landscapes. Walk through towering sandstone cliffs, uncover monuments carved directly into rock, and explore hidden trails that reveal the city’s remarkable history. From the iconic Treasury to peaceful canyon paths, Petra offers an unforgettable journey through time.

highlights.title: The Treasury — Al-Khazneh
highlights.description: Petra’s most famous ancient façade, carved into rose-coloured rock, is the city’s iconic landmark.

highlights.title: The Siq
highlights.description: A narrow natural rock passage stretching for more than a kilometre, with an unforgettable reveal of the Treasury at its end.

highlights.title: The Monastery — Ad-Deir
highlights.description: A monumental ancient façade set among the mountains, reached by a long staircase—ideal for walking and adventure enthusiasts.

highlights.title: The Royal Tombs
highlights.description: A group of royal tombs carved into the mountainside, distinguished by their colourful rock and unique façade details.

highlights.title: Street of Facades
highlights.description: A row of rock-carved façades and tombs along the route leading into the heart of the ancient city.

highlights.title: Little Petra — Siq Al-Barid
highlights.description: A smaller, quieter Nabataean site with narrow passages, rock façades, and chambers carved into the mountains.

highlights.title: High Place of Sacrifice
highlights.description: Climb to an ancient Nabataean ritual site with sweeping views across Petra’s mountains and valleys.

highlights.title: The Cave Experience
highlights.description: Discover Bedouin life inside a cave and enjoy Arabic coffee, kohl and henna traditions, depending on the experience available.

highlights.title: The Great Temple
highlights.description: An extensive archaeological complex with columns, courtyards, and Nabataean structures that reveal aspects of civic life in the ancient city.

highlights.title: Arabic Coffee & Bedouin Hospitality
highlights.description: Experience Arabic coffee and discover the traditions of Bedouin hospitality.

facts.label: Entrance Fee
facts.value: 1 JOD Jordanians · 30 JOD Arabs · 50–90 JOD foreigners

wadiRum.name: Wadi Rum
wadiRum.about: Wadi Rum is a breathtaking desert landscape known for its red sand, dramatic mountains and unforgettable adventure experiences.

highlights.title: Hot Air Balloon
highlights.description: Soar above Wadi Rum at sunrise and admire its vast red-sand valleys, towering sandstone mountains, and breathtaking desert scenery from the sky.

highlights.title: Bedouin Dinner Experience
highlights.description: Taste traditional Bedouin food, including zarb cooked underground, and discover local hospitality and customs.

highlights.title: Khazali Canyon
highlights.description: Walk through a narrow sandstone canyon and discover ancient inscriptions and rock carvings.

highlights.title: Burdah Rock Bridge
highlights.description: Admire one of Wadi Rum’s most impressive natural arches. Reaching the top involves a challenging scramble and should be done with an experienced local guide.

highlights.title: Sandboarding
highlights.description: Slide down the soft red sand dunes for a fun desert adventure.

facts.label: Guided Tours
facts.value: Local 4×4 Driver for Exploring the Protected Area

ajlounCastle.name: Ajloun Castle
ajlounCastle.about: Ajloun Castle, also known as Qal’at ar-Rabad, is a medieval Islamic fortress overlooking the green hills of northern Jordan. Built in 1184 by Izz al-Din Usama, one of Saladin’s commanders, it served as a strategic stronghold against Crusader expansion and helped protect important trade routes. With its stone towers, vaulted halls, and panoramic views, the castle offers a fascinating glimpse into Jordan’s medieval history.

highlights.title: Hidden Stone Corridors
highlights.description: Look for the vaulted passages, narrow openings, and defensive features that reveal how the fortress was designed for protection.

facts.label: Built By & Age
facts.value: Izz al-Din Usama · Built in 1184 AD · Over 840 Years Old

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.25 JOD for Jordanians · 3 JOD for Foreigners

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Optional · Explore at Your Own Pace

ajlounRelax.name: Ajloun Forest Reserve
ajlounRelax.about: Ajloun Forest Reserve is a beautiful nature destination in northern Jordan, known for its rolling green hills, oak woodlands, and diverse wildlife. Visitors can explore scenic hiking trails, discover local traditions, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of one of Jordan’s most charming forest landscapes.

highlights.title: Hike Through the Forest
highlights.description: Follow scenic woodland trails and enjoy peaceful views beneath the oak trees.

highlights.title: Try a Forest Adventure
highlights.description: Experience the thrill of ziplining above the forest, subject to availability.

highlights.title: Discover Local Traditions
highlights.description: Visit the Soap House in nearby Orjan village and learn about traditional olive-oil soap making.

highlights.title: Enjoy a Nature Escape
highlights.description: Slow down, breathe in the fresh mountain air, and enjoy a peaceful day surrounded by greenery.

highlights.title: Teleferic Ajloun
highlights.description: Enjoy a scenic ride above Ajloun’s lush green hills, with panoramic views of the forests and Ajloun Castle.

ajlounRelax.tagline: Green Trails · Fresh Air · Nature Escape
ajlounRelax.visitNote: Spring is especially beautiful when wildflowers bloom across the forest.

aqabaAdventures.name: Aqaba Adventures
aqabaAdventures.about: Aqaba offers exciting adventures in the Red Sea, from diving and snorkeling to boat trips and water activities.

aqaba.name: Aqaba Relaxation
aqaba.about:
Aqaba is Jordan’s seaside escape, where the clear waters of the Red Sea meet beautiful beaches and mountain views. From relaxing by the shore to enjoying peaceful boat cruises, the city offers the perfect setting to slow down and recharge.

Whether you're watching the sunset over the water or enjoying the gentle sea breeze, Aqaba invites you to experience Jordan at a more relaxed pace.

highlights.title: Explore Coral Gardens
highlights.description: Swim or dive among colorful coral formations and observe the rich biodiversity of Aqaba’s Red Sea.

highlights.title: Sunset Yacht Cruise
highlights.description: Watch the sun set over the Red Sea from the deck of a yacht, surrounded by warm evening light.

highlights.title: Explore the Fishermen’s Harbour
highlights.description: Take a relaxed stroll by the traditional harbor and watch local fishermen bring in their catch.

highlights.title: Aqaba Water Adventures
highlights.description: From thrilling jet ski rides and parasailing to yacht cruises and underwater discoveries, explore the best of the Red Sea and find your perfect sea escape.

packing: Bring swimwear and a beach towel.
Bring a hat and lightweight clothing.
Bring snorkeling gear, if you have your own.
aqaba.visitTip: Check beach access and day-pass requirements before visiting private beach clubs.

wadiMujib.name: Wadi Mujib
wadiMujib.about: Wadi Mujib is a spectacular canyon in Jordan known for its dramatic landscapes, flowing water trails and exciting adventure experiences.

highlights.title: Ibex Trail
highlights.description: Follow a mountain trail overlooking the Dead Sea, with opportunities to spot Nubian ibex and enjoy panoramic views.

main.name: Ma'in Hot Springs
main.about: Ma'in Hot Springs is a beautiful natural destination famous for its warm mineral waterfalls, relaxing atmosphere and stunning mountain scenery.

highlights.title: Relax in the Hot Springs
highlights.description: Unwind in naturally heated mineral-water pools surrounded by dramatic cliffs

packing: Bring dry clothes to change into after enjoying the springs.
Keep your essentials protected from splashes.
Keep your phone dry around the springs.
Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat.
Keep fresh drinking water with you.
Bring swimwear and a towel for your visit.

jerash.name: Jerash
jerash.about: Jerash is one of Jordan’s most remarkable historical destinations, known for its exceptionally well-preserved Roman ruins. Once known as Gerasa, the ancient city flourished under Roman rule and became an important regional centre. Today, visitors can explore its colonnaded streets, monumental temples, ancient theatres, and public squares while experiencing the rich history and culture of northern Jordan.

highlights.title: Explore the Roman City
highlights.description: Walk through ancient streets, grand plazas, temples, and impressive Roman architecture that reveal the city’s fascinating past.

highlights.title: Visit the Ancient Theatres
highlights.description: Discover the South and North Theatres and imagine the performances and gatherings that once filled these historic spaces.

highlights.title: The Nymphaeum
highlights.description: Discover an impressive Roman public fountain built in 191 AD, once decorated with marble and water features.

highlights.title: Cardo Maximus
highlights.description: Follow the ancient paved main street, where original stones and column-lined walkways preserve traces of Roman city life.

highlights.title: Jerash Archaeological Museum
highlights.description: Explore artifacts and archaeological discoveries that reveal the civilizations that shaped the region.

facts.label: Built By
facts.value: Ancient Greeks · Flourished Under Roman Rule

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.50 JOD for Jordanians · 10 JOD for Foreigners

ummQais.name: Umm Qais
ummQais.about: Umm Qais, once known as Gadara, is a remarkable archaeological destination in northern Jordan. As one of the cities of the ancient Decapolis, it flourished under Roman rule and became known for its cultural and intellectual life. Today, visitors can explore black basalt ruins, ancient theatres, colonnaded streets, and an Ottoman-era village while enjoying breathtaking views of the Jordan Valley and the Sea of Galilee.

highlights.title: Visit Umm Qais Museum
highlights.description: Discover ancient pottery, statues, mosaics, and other archaeological finds displayed in a restored Ottoman-era house.

highlights.title: Beekeeping Experience
highlights.description: Learn how local beekeepers care for their hives and produce honey, with opportunities to discover the process up close.

highlights.title: The Octagonal Church
highlights.description: Explore the remains of a Byzantine-era church and discover another layer of the site’s religious history.

highlights.title: The Nymphaeum
highlights.description: Look for the remains of an ancient public fountain among the archaeological structures of Gadara.

facts.label: Built By & Age
facts.value: Hellenistic Origins · Flourished Under Roman Rule

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.25 JOD for Jordanians · 5 JOD for Foreigners

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Optional · Explore at Your Own Pace

danaReserve.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
danaReserve.about: Dana Biosphere Reserve is Jordan’s largest biosphere reserve, covering approximately 292 km² of diverse landscapes, from mountain peaks and terraced gardens to deep canyons and desert valleys. Established in 1989, it is home to a remarkable variety of plants and wildlife. Visitors can explore scenic hiking trails, discover traditional village life, and experience the natural beauty and biodiversity of Jordan.

highlights.title: Wildlife Watching
highlights.description: Discover Dana’s remarkable wildlife, from the Nubian ibex and mountain gazelles to foxes and diverse bird species. Keep your eyes open as you explore the reserve’s rugged mountains and natural habitats.

highlights.title: Wadi Dana Hike
highlights.description: Explore deep sandstone canyons and diverse natural landscapes on a long scenic hike toward Feynan.

highlights.title: Rummana Mountain Trail
highlights.description: Enjoy a scenic walk with mountain views, striking rock formations, and opportunities for birdwatching.

highlights.title: The Caves Trail
highlights.description: Explore unusual sandstone formations and small caves hidden among the rocky landscape.

karakCastle.name: Karak Castle
karakCastle.about: Perched on a hilltop overlooking the city of Al Karak, Karak Castle is one of Jordan’s most impressive medieval fortresses. Built in the 12th century during the Crusader period, the castle later became an important stronghold under Muslim rule. Its massive stone walls, underground passages, vaulted halls, and strategic location reveal centuries of military history. Today, visitors can explore its remarkable architecture and enjoy sweeping views of the surrounding landscape.

highlights.title: Panorama Al-Karak Restaurant & Café
highlights.description: Enjoy a breathtaking view of Karak Castle while experiencing local flavors and authentic Jordanian hospitality.

highlights.title: Discover Underground Passages
highlights.description: Explore the castle’s historic lower levels and learn how its architecture supported medieval defense.

highlights.title: Visit the Castle Museum
highlights.description: Discover archaeological finds and exhibits that tell the story of the castle and the region.

highlights.title: Make Mansaf & Jameed
highlights.description: Discover Karak’s culinary heritage by learning how traditional jameed is made and taking part in preparing Jordan’s famous mansaf. Experience authentic local flavors and the traditions behind one of Jordan’s most iconic dishes.

packing: Pack a light jacket for cooler months.

dibeenForest.name: Dibeen Forest
dibeenForest.about: Dibeen Forest Reserve is a beautiful natural escape in northern Jordan, near Jerash. Established in 2004, the reserve protects a unique Mediterranean forest dominated by Aleppo pine and evergreen oak trees. Its rolling hills, rich plant diversity, and peaceful woodland atmosphere make it an ideal destination for nature lovers, families, and visitors seeking a relaxing outdoor experience.

highlights.title: Forest Walks
highlights.description: Wander among tall pine and oak trees, breathe in the fresh air, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of the forest.

highlights.title: Wildlife & Birdwatching
highlights.description: Look and listen for woodland birds and local wildlife, including the Persian squirrel, which is one of the reserve’s notable species.

highlights.title: Beeswax Candle-Making
highlights.description: Explore a creative workshop that transforms beeswax into handmade candles, supporting local crafts and community initiatives. Confirm booking and session times.

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Not Required for General Visits · Check Trail Requirements

romanTheater.name: Roman Theater
romanTheater.about: The Roman Theatre is one of Amman’s most iconic historical landmarks, dating back to the 2nd century AD when the city was known as Philadelphia. Built into a hillside, this impressive stone theatre could host around 6,000 spectators. Its steep seating tiers were designed to provide excellent views and acoustics. Today, it remains a symbol of Jordan’s Roman heritage and continues to host cultural performances and events.

highlights.title: Explore the Theatre
highlights.description: Climb the ancient seating tiers and admire the impressive architecture and panoramic views of Downtown Amman.

highlights.title: Visit the Museums
highlights.description: Discover Jordanian traditional clothing, jewellery, and cultural heritage at the museums housed within the theatre complex.

highlights.title: Cultural Events
highlights.description: Experience concerts and cultural performances when events are scheduled at this historic venue.

facts.label: Built By & Age
facts.value: Romans · 2nd Century AD · Around 1,800 Years Old

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.25 JOD for Jordanians · 2 JOD for Foreigners

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Optional · Explore at Your Own Pace

nearbyCards.name: Rainbow Street
nearbyCards.description: Explore cafés, restaurants, small shops, and the lively atmosphere of Jabal Amman.

nearbyCards.name: Downtown Amman
nearbyCards.description: Wander through traditional markets and try local favourites such as falafel, hummus, and kunafa.

shobak.name: Shobak
shobak.about: Shobak is a beautiful mountain destination known for its historic landscapes, hiking trails and breathtaking views. It offers an amazing experience for adventure and nature lovers.

afra.name: Afra Hot Springs
afra.about: Afra Hot Springs is a natural thermal destination located approximately 26 km north of Tafila city in Jordan. The area features more than 15 hot-water springs, with mineral-rich waters flowing through a rocky valley to form streams and small waterfalls. Surrounded by rugged landscapes, Afra offers visitors an opportunity to relax in warm pools, enjoy nature, and experience one of southern Jordan’s distinctive natural attractions.

highlights.description: Unwind in naturally heated mineral waters surrounded by rocky landscapes and flowing streams.
highlights.title: Relax at Afra Hot Springs

highlights.description: Escape to cozy eco-friendly huts surrounded by Dana’s breathtaking mountains. Enjoy peaceful views, fresh air, and a relaxing stay immersed in nature.
highlights.title: Dana Luxury Huts – Eco Lodge

highlights.description: Discover scenic hiking trails, dramatic mountain landscapes, and the rich biodiversity of Jordan's largest nature reserve.
highlights.title: Explore Dana Nature Reserve

highlights.description: Discover the history and cultural heritage of Tafila through its archaeological treasures and local traditions.
highlights.title: Explore Tafila's Heritage

packing: Bring water shoes for slippery surfaces.
Bring a waterproof bag for personal belongings.
afra.safetyTip: Spring water can be extremely hot near its source, and rocks may be slippery. Use designated bathing areas only.
afra.tagline: Natural Warmth · Mineral Waters · Pure Relaxation

mukawir.name: Mukawir Castle
mukawir.about: Mukawir Castle is an ancient hilltop fortress built in the 1st century BC. It is historically associated with Herod Antipas and the story of John the Baptist. Today, its ruins offer breathtaking views of the Dead Sea region.

quickInfo.access: Car recommended · Uphill walk to the ruins

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.value: Car recommended · Uphill walk to the ruins

packing: Wear sturdy shoes for the rocky uphill path.
Stay hydrated, especially on warm days.
Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat.
Capture the ancient ruins and panoramic Dead Sea views.
Keep your phone charged for photos and navigation.

highlights.title: Explore the Ruins
highlights.description: Walk among the remains of the ancient hilltop fortress and discover its history.

highlights.title: Enjoy the Views
highlights.description: Take in panoramic views of the Dead Sea and surrounding mountains.

highlights.title: Discover the History
highlights.description: Uncover the stories of an ancient fortress linked to Herod Antipas and the history of John the Baptist.

wadiZarqaMain.name: Wadi Zarqa Ma'in
wadiZarqaMain.about:
Wadi Zarqa Ma'in is a striking natural valley near the Dead Sea, known for its rugged cliffs, flowing stream, and dramatic desert landscapes. It offers an adventurous escape for travelers who want to explore Jordan beyond its famous tourist destinations.

With scenic hiking routes and untouched natural surroundings, the wadi is ideal for discovering a wilder side of Jordan.

info.bestTime: Dry weather · Confirm conditions with a guide

highlights.title: Hike Through the Wadi
highlights.description: Explore rugged terrain and follow scenic trails through the dramatic canyon landscape

highlights.title: Upper Waterfall Abseiling
highlights.description: Descend dramatic waterfalls using ropes and professional canyoning equipment, surrounded by the rugged beauty of Wadi Zarqa Ma'in

highlights.title: Discover the Natural Stream
highlights.description: Experience the beauty of flowing water winding through rocky cliffs and wild surroundings

packing: Pack snacks and a small backpack.
Bring a fully charged phone and power bank.
wadiZarqaMain.cardDescription: Discover a hidden world of dramatic cliffs, flowing water, and wild beauty in the heart of Jordan.
wadiZarqaMain.safetyTip: Hire a licensed local guide, check weather conditions before your trip, and avoid the wadi during rain or flash-flood warnings.

madabaPark.name: Madaba Archaeological Park
madabaPark.about: Madaba Archaeological Park is a historic site in the heart of Madaba, showcasing remarkable Roman and Byzantine ruins and ancient mosaics. Explore centuries of Jordan’s cultural heritage in one place.

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.value: Easy access · Located in central Madaba

packing: Walk comfortably around the archaeological site.
Capture the mosaics and historical details.
Keep your phone charged for photos and navigation.

highlights.title: Admire Ancient Mosaics
highlights.description: Discover intricate Byzantine mosaic floors depicting figures, flowers, birds, and scenes from ancient mythology

highlights.title: Walk Through Roman History
highlights.description: Follow the remains of an ancient Roman street surrounded by historic stonework and archaeological ruins

highlights.title: Discover Ancient Churches
highlights.description: Explore the remains of early churches and uncover the religious heritage of Byzantine Madaba

highlights.title: Explore Mosaic Art
highlights.description: Observe the detailed patterns and craftsmanship that made Madaba famous as the City of Mosaics

aqabaFort.name: Aqaba Fort
aqabaFort.about: Aqaba Fort, also known as Aqaba Castle, is a historic fortress near the shores of the Red Sea. Its origins are linked to the Mamluk period, and it was later renovated and used during Ottoman rule as a military stronghold and caravanserai. The fort played an important role in regional trade and became associated with the Arab Revolt in 1917. Today, visitors can explore its historic stone architecture and discover an important chapter of Jordan’s history.

facts.label: Built By & Age
facts.value: Mamluk Origins · Current Form Mainly Dates to the 16th Century

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.25 JOD for Jordanians · 3 JOD for Foreigners

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Optional · Explore at Your Own Pace

highlights.title: Explore the Fortress
highlights.description: Walk through the historic stone courtyard, arches, and fortified walls while discovering the castle’s military past.

highlights.title: Historic Waterfront Walk
highlights.description: Combine your visit with a relaxing walk along the nearby waterfront and enjoy views of the Red Sea.

nearbyCards.name: Sharif Hussein bin Ali House
nearbyCards.description: Visit a heritage house connected to Sharif Hussein bin Ali and the history of the Arab Revolt.

nearbyCards.name: Great Arab Revolt Plaza
nearbyCards.description: Visit the nearby waterfront square commemorating the Great Arab Revolt.

ummAlJimal.name: Umm Al-Jimal
ummAlJimal.tagline: Also known as the Black Oasis
ummAlJimal.about: Umm Al-Jimal is an extraordinary archaeological site in northern Jordan, famous for its distinctive black basalt buildings and remarkably preserved ruins. Once an important settlement during the Nabataean, Roman, Byzantine, and early Islamic periods, it offers a glimpse into ancient life through its stone houses, churches, courtyards, and historic structures. Its unique architecture and peaceful desert surroundings make it a fascinating destination for history and culture lovers.

info.nearby: Azraq Wetland Reserve · Shaumari Wildlife Reserve

quickInfo.access: Check Current Ticket Prices Before Visiting

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: Check Current Ticket Prices Before Visiting

highlights.title: Travel Through History
highlights.description: Learn about the Nabataean, Roman, Byzantine, and early Islamic periods that shaped Umm Al-Jimal.

highlights.title: Basalt Stone Carving
highlights.description: Try carving basalt stone with the help of a local instructor and create a small artwork as a souvenir of your journey.

highlights.title: Bedouin Cultural Experience
highlights.description: Experience Bedouin hospitality, taste Arabic coffee, and listen to folk stories and local traditions. The experience may include the rababa.

highlights.title: Umm Al-Jimal Museum
highlights.description: Explore archaeological finds and discover the history and cultural heritage of Umm Al-Jimal through its historic artifacts and local stories.

azraqWetland.name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
azraqWetland.about: Located in Jordan’s eastern desert, Azraq Wetland Reserve is a unique natural oasis famous for its freshwater pools, marshlands, and rich biodiversity. Established in 1977, the reserve is an important stop for migratory birds traveling between Europe, Asia, and Africa. Visitors can explore peaceful wooden walkways, observe wildlife, and discover the conservation efforts protecting one of Jordan’s most valuable wetland ecosystems.

highlights.title: Walk the Marsh Trail
highlights.description: Explore the wetland landscape along wooden walkways and peaceful nature trails.

highlights.title: Birdwatching
highlights.description: Observe migratory and resident birds in one of Jordan’s most important wetland habitats.

highlights.title: Water Buffalo Trail
highlights.description: Walk a trail through wetlands and wildlife observation areas, with a chance to see water buffalo if they are present during your visit.

shaumariReserve.name: Shaumari Wildlife Reserve
shaumariReserve.about: Located near Azraq in Jordan’s eastern desert, Shaumari Wildlife Reserve was established in 1975 as Jordan’s first wildlife reserve. Covering approximately 22 square kilometers, it plays an important role in protecting endangered species and restoring native wildlife. The reserve is especially known for the Arabian oryx, alongside gazelles and other desert animals. It offers visitors a unique opportunity to discover Jordan’s wildlife and conservation efforts in a natural desert setting.

highlights.title: Oryx Safari
highlights.description: Explore the reserve on a guided safari and look for the iconic Arabian oryx and other wildlife.

highlights.title: Wildlife Discovery Centre
highlights.description: Explore educational exhibits about endangered animals, Arabian oryx conservation programmes, and wildlife reintroduction.

highlights.title: Wildlife Watching
highlights.description: Observe Arabian oryx, gazelles, and other animals in their protected environment.

wadiBinHammad.name: Wadi Bin Hammad
wadiBinHammad.about: Located near Al-Karak in Jordan, Wadi Bin Hammad is a beautiful canyon known for its flowing streams, natural hot springs, waterfalls, and lush vegetation. The trail winds through narrow rocky passages surrounded by palm trees and hanging greenery, creating a refreshing contrast to the surrounding dry landscape. It is an ideal destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers looking to experience water hiking and explore one of Jordan’s hidden natural gems.
packing: Wear water shoes with good grip.
Protect electronics in a waterproof bag.

highlights.title: Water Hiking
highlights.description: Follow the stream through the canyon, walking through shallow water and rocky passages.

highlights.title: Discover the Hot Springs
highlights.description: See the mineral-rich springs flowing through the rocky landscape near the entrance.

highlights.title: Canyon Photography
highlights.description: Capture dramatic rock formations, flowing water, and greenery hidden between the cliffs.

ammanCitadel.name: Amman Citadel
ammanCitadel.about: Perched on one of Amman’s highest hills, the Amman Citadel is an extraordinary archaeological site that reflects thousands of years of Jordanian history. Once the heart of ancient Rabbath-Ammon, it preserves traces of Ammonite, Roman, Byzantine, and Islamic civilizations. Visitors can explore monumental ruins, discover the famous Temple of Hercules, and enjoy panoramic views of Downtown Amman.

facts.label: Built By & Age
facts.value: Ammonites & Successive Civilizations · Over 3,000 Years of History

facts.label: Entry Fee
facts.value: 0.25 JOD for Jordanians · 3 JOD for Foreigners

facts.label: Guided Tour
facts.value: Optional · Explore at Your Own Pace

highlights.title: Temple of Hercules
highlights.description: Admire the monumental Roman columns and the remains of one of the Citadel’s most iconic landmarks.

highlights.title: Umayyad Palace
highlights.description: Explore the remains of an early Islamic palace complex known for its distinctive architecture and historic significance.

highlights.title: Byzantine Church
highlights.description: Discover the remains of an ancient church and learn about the Byzantine period in Amman.

highlights.title: Jordan Archaeological Museum
highlights.description: Discover archaeological objects that reveal the story of Jordan’s ancient civilizations.

nearbyCards.name: Rainbow Street
nearbyCards.description: Explore cafés, restaurants, small shops, and the lively atmosphere of Jabal Amman.

nearbyCards.name: Downtown Amman
nearbyCards.description: Wander through traditional markets and try local favourites such as falafel, hummus, and kunafa.
